edges.description: Perturbed HOXA13 transcription-factor activity disrupts patterning of the distal limb bud.
The same HOXA13 defect disrupts development of the distal male urethra.
Preaxial deficiency of the hand manifests as hypoplastic thumbs.
Preaxial deficiency of the foot manifests as hypoplastic great toes.
Abnormal ulnar-side autopod patterning produces supernumerary postaxial digits of the hands.
Reduced phalangeal patterning produces uniphalangeal, shortened second toes.
Distal toe patterning failure leaves the second toes without nails.
Disrupted distal male urethral patterning produces glanular hypospadias.

nodes.description: Absent nails of the affected (second) toes.

nodes.description: Loss of normal HOXA13-dependent regionalization of the autopod produces the combined preaxial deficiency and postaxial polydactyly of the hands and the distal foot anomalies. The mechanistic link from HOXA13 dysfunction to limb patterning is inferred from HOXA13's established role in distal limb morphogenesis; the limb abnormalities themselves are observed in the family.

nodes.description: HOXA13 also patterns the distal genitourinary tract; its dysfunction disrupts male urethral development, producing glanular hypospadias in affected males. The genital abnormality is observed; the HOXA13-dependent mechanism is inferred.

evidence.reference_title: A HOXA13 allele with a missense mutation in the homeobox and a dinucleotide deletion in the promoter underlies Guttmacher syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Guttmacher syndrome, a dominantly inherited combination of distal limb and genital tract abnormalities, has several features in common with hand-foot-genital syndrome (HFGS), including hypoplastic first digits and hypospadias.

nodes.description: Glanular hypospadias (ventrally displaced urethral opening at the glans) in affected males.

evidence.snippet: Both males also had glandular hypospadias.

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense variant in the HOXA13 homeobox (c.1112A>T, Q50L) alters a key residue in the recognition helix of the homeodomain and is predicted to perturb the DNA-binding transcription-factor activity of HOXA13, with both a loss and a specific gain of function. The variant arose on an allele also carrying a 2-bp deletion in the gene's conserved promoter; that deletion produces no abnormality on its own but may contribute to the phenotype.
